title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Sewell Wallis are currently working with a fast-paced South Yorkshire retail business who are now looking for an Accounts Assistant to join their finance team in North Sheffield. This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment, takes pride in getting the detail right and is confident managing a varied transactional finance workload.

You'll play an important role in supporting the day-to-day finance function, taking ownership of transactional finance, while also having the chance to be involved in month-end processes and financial reporting.

What will you be doing?

You'll be providing day-to-day support across a broad range of accounts assistant duties, including:
- Performing daily reconciliations of company bank accounts
- Processing supplier invoices and credit notes, matching invoices to purchase orders and goods received, and maintaining an accurate purchase ledger.
- Obtaining and reconciling monthly supplier statements, investigating disputed invoices and liaising with suppliers to resolve queries.
- Reviewing and monitoring purchase orders and setting up new supplier accounts, ensuring bank details are verified in line with company procedures.
- Reviewing credit card expenditure and ensuring expenses are correctly coded and supported by the appropriate documentation.
- Supporting month-end processes, including accruals, prepayments, fixed asset accounting and balance sheet reconciliations.
- Assisting with financial analysis, reporting and the preparation of management accounts as your experience develops.
- Gaining exposure to audit and VAT-related processes while continuing to develop your technical accounting knowledge.

What skills are we looking for?
- Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including the confident use of SUMIFS and XLOOKUP and/or VLOOKUP.
- A good understanding of purchase ledger processes, supplier invoices and payment runs.
- Strong attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining accurate financial records.
- Strong communication skills

What's on offer?
- A competitive Salary of c 30000
- Excellent long-term progression opportunities
- Pension Contribution

Apply below or contact Jemima for more information.

To apply, please send your CV, quoting our reference and specifying which website you saw this position advertised on. Due to the high volume of applications, please accept that if we have not responded to your application within seven days, your application has not been successful. Sewell Wallis is a specialist recruitment company with a vast amount of experience in our industry. We offer permanent, temporary and interim recruitment support for accounting and finance, human resources and business support positions. We recruit at all levels within finance, from Purchase Ledger Administrator and Credit Controller level through to Financial Controller and Director positions. We are well situated to cover all of South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire and Manchester. Please visit our website for more information on accountancy and finance jobs and human resources or business support positions.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Working within the Reward team, the Payroll Administrator will support the delivery of the payroll for the various legal entities in Klipboard. As the payroll administrator, you will play a crucial role in managing and administering payroll and pension processes. Your primary responsibility will be to ensure accurate and timely processing of payroll, compliance with statutory regulations, and efficient administration of pension schemes. This role requires a deep understanding of UK payroll and pension regulations, strong attention to detail, and excellent organizational skills

Key Responsibilities:
- Process and coordinate monthly payroll activities, ensuring all payroll inputs are accurately captured, including new starters, leavers, contractual changes, sickness, maternity, paternity, overtime, and shift payments.
- Administer statutory payments and entitlements, including SSP, SMP, and SPP, and provide employees with guidance on eligibility and benefits.
- Conduct payroll reconciliations and validation checks to ensure payroll accuracy, completeness, and compliance with statutory requirements.
- Maintain accurate payroll, pension, benefits, and employee records across payroll and HR systems.
- Calculate and process salary increases, overtime payments, shift allowances, and other pay adjustments in accordance with company policies and contractual requirements.
- Prepare and deliver payroll-related reports, analysis, and management information to support HR, Finance, and business requirements.
- Reconcile and maintain data between payroll, HRIS, pension, and other related systems to ensure consistency and accuracy.
- Prepare and submit payroll information and statutory reports to HMRC, pension providers, and other relevant bodies in line with reporting requirements.
- Administer pension schemes and employee benefit programmes, including enrolment, contribution management, and query resolution.
- Monitor, investigate, and resolve payroll audit exceptions, discrepancies, and data anomalies in a timely manner.
- Ensure all payroll transactions are processed in compliance with payroll legislation, tax regulations, National Insurance requirements, and company policies.
- Act as a key point of contact for employees, providing clear and accurate advice on payroll, taxation, pensions, benefits, and related queries.
- Support internal and external payroll, pension, and compliance audits, ensuring accurate documentation and audit trails are maintained.
- Collaborate closely with HR, Finance, pension providers, and external stakeholders to ensure efficient payroll operations and regulatory compliance.
- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of payroll, taxation, pension, and employment legislation to ensure ongoing compliance and best practice.
- Identify opportunities to improve payroll processes, controls, reporting, and service delivery, contributing to continuous improvement initiatives.
- Support compliance inspections, PAYE reviews, pension audits, and other regulatory requirements as necessary.
- Undertake additional payroll, reporting, and administrative responsibilities as required in line with the scope and level of the role.

Skills, Knowledge and Experience:
- Strong numeracy and high attention to detail
- Competence with and experience of payroll systems and procedures.
- A strong eye for detail with an innate desire for accuracy
- Proficient in effective collaboration with internal and external stakeholders
- Ability to take responsibility for own work.
- Ability to maintain absolute discretion and maturity in handling sensitive/confidential data.
- Excellent time management skills with a proven ability to meet tight deadlines.
- High standards of work and performance.
- Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite to include intermediate Excel skills (Pivot Tables,
- V-Lookups, etc.)
- Effective team player with a 'can do' attitude.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills

The Payroll Officer will be responsible for the collation of time and attendance records and ensuring that employees' timecards are complete. You will investigate any instances of non-attendance before submitting records to the partners for payment processing.

Key Deliverables
- Act as the primary on-site payroll focal point for all blue-collar personnel up to and including the Superintendent level.

- Coordinate payroll activity utilizing the Kronos Time and Attendance system in accordance with approved procedures.

- Maintain a detailed log of personnel related to query resolutions.
- Manage the Kronos system workflow, including adding new starters and removing leavers.

- Receive and input absence (sickness) records provided by the supervisory team.

Key Requirements / Qualifications
- Education: NVQ Level 3 or equivalent qualification, or demonstrated capability via a competency-based assessment/interview.
